http://www.euronews.com/2026/07/30/drone.text: A drone struck a US-owned liquefied natural gas vessel at Egypt's Mediterranean port of Damietta on Wednesday, triggering a fire that spread to a second ship, in what would be the first attack on Egyptian soil since the war between Iran and the US began in February.Egypt's cabinet confirmed on Thursday morning that "preliminary investigations by the relevant authorities found that the incident was caused by a drone," making it the first official confirmation of the attack's nature.No side has claimed responsibility at this time, and an investigation remains ongoing.In the meantime, authorities were taking measures "to protect Egypt's interests and national security," the cabinet said.Egypt's Petroleum Ministry had earlier confirmed the fire without identifying the cause. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi travelled to the port to oversee the response.The drone struck the Energos Winter, a Marshall Islands-flagged floating storage and regasification unit owned by US company New Fortress Energy, on its starboard side at approximately 3:20 pm CET, according to maritime security firm Ambrey and British firm Vanguard.The fire spread to the nearby Bermuda-flagged LNG tanker Gaslog Salem. Both crews were evacuated. The fire was brought under control and no injuries were reported. Both vessels were subsequently moved offshore for assessment.Tehran touts map of targetsEgyptian authorities and multiple maritime sources confirmed that Iranian state television had identified Damietta as a possible target for "retaliation against Ukrainian interests" two days earlier, following a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea over the weekend.The map shown on state-run TV described Damietta as "a gateway for gas exports to Europe." Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Tuesday that Iran "does not seek escalation" but was demanding "compensation" from Kyiv.Energy analytics firm Kpler said the attack disrupted operations at the terminal and forced both vessels to move offshore.Former head of the Damietta Port Authority, Major General Ayman Salah, said that the regasification process occurs at very high pressure and that any leak could cause a fire.The incident comes as the region enters one of its most volatile periods since the war began.On Wednesday, the IRGC launched ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan, the US and Saudi Arabia struck Iran-linked militia sites across Iraq, and Yemen's Houthi group declared a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, raising fears of the widest simultaneous regional escalation since the war began on 28 February.Egypt has so far been spared from attacks during the US-Iran war, maintaining relations with both Washington and Tehran.Egypt's Suez Canal, through which roughly 12% of global trade normally passes, has already seen a dramatic drop in traffic since the war began.It is now further imperilled by the reported plans by Yemen's Houthi group to impose a toll on passing cargo ships and threats of strikes on noncompliant vessels, which could severely reduce the traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait in the Red Sea.Egypt had previously been an LNG exporter — Damietta hosted one of the Arabic-speaking world's first LNG export terminals — but declining domestic gas production turned the country into a net importer.

Photograph: Clarens Siffroy/AFP/Getty Images Haiti At least 47 killed and dozens kidnapped in gang attack near Haiti capital Gang leader threatens to kill hostages after attack in Kenscoff in which homes were also set alight ‘A massacre’: Haiti gangs carrying out mass killings Associated Press in Port-au-Prince Tue 25 Aug 2026 13.35 EDT Last modified on Tue 25 Aug 2026 13.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped when armed men attacked a once peaceful community near Haiti’s capital at the weekend, the UN has said. A gang leader has threatened to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community of Kenscoff, nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince. Sunday’s attack pierced the belief that security in the Caribbean country was improving. Romain Le Cour, the head of Haiti observatory at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, said: “This is a major political and security test – for the government, for the police and for the international mission alike.” In a video posted on social media, the gang leader warned the director of Haiti’s national police, Vladimir Paraison, not to use drones to repel gangs in the area. “Paraison, if any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them,” he said, referring to the hostages. He identified himself as Izo 2, a reference to Izo, or Johnson André, one of Haiti’s most powerful gang members. Le Cour said Izo 2 was also known as Didi and led the armed group in Kenscoff on behalf of and in coordination with Izo and other gang leaders. “He’s running a kind of franchise cell for other gangs,” he said. Le Cour said the aim of the attack could be to force Haiti’s police and the UN-backed gang suppression force to disperse even more of their limited resources. “They don’t have enough personnel,” he said. “If you force them to deploy more troops, it would inevitably be at the expense of other areas.” The attack may also be a show of force and a message to Haiti’s government and police as the country prepares to hold general elections on 13 December, the first in more than a decade. Le Cour said: “This is a message to the government and the police that their claims of protection do not match reality. The gangs are saying: when we choose to attack, we can, and we will succeed.” View image in fullscreen Women mourn at the site of the attack in Kenscoff. Photograph: Patrice Noel/Reuters The first major attack on Kenscoff occurred in January 2025 and since then there have been sporadic attacks in the mountains surrounding the city centre. Sunday’s attack was the largest yet. At least five of the 47 people killed were children, according to the UN integrated office in Haiti, known as BINUH. Guns, gangs and drought: how crime and the climate crisis are reshaping Haiti Read more Kenscoff’s mayor, Jean Massillon, said two government employees were among those killed, including his cousin who served as his security detail. He said members of Viv Ansanm, a powerful gang coalition that the US has designated as a foreign terrorist organisation, also set fire to 25 homes. Massillon said gangs were still roaming Kenscoff’s periphery. “The atrocity of this crime reminds us that we have to continue working stronger every day to bring peace to the community,” he said. “I’m optimistic that the state will continue working to eradicate the gangs in Kenscoff.” Some survivors accused the government of not providing enough protection before the attack. The police rejected the accusations. Le Cour said that if police and armoured vehicles were indeed stationed in Kenscoff before the attack, it was concerning. “You let the gangs come in even if you had everything in place?” he said. Armed men control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince and swaths of land in Haiti’s central region and beyond, and gang violence has displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti. More than 3,050 people were reported killed from January to June and another 1,400 injured, according to UN statistics released on Tuesday. Property Forum 2026 looks ahead to the market’s future Autor: oprac. dz Dodano: 06 wrz 2026 17:32 Dodaj do zaufanych źródeł w Google Dzięki temu zobaczysz w Google więcej informacji od portalu PropertyNews.pl Real estate must be ready for change. Property Forum 2026 looks ahead to the market’s future The central question linking the debates during Property Forum 2026 will be what types of real estate can retain their value amid economic, technological and demographic change. Studio PTWP Skomentuj (0) Podziel się Twittnij Udostępnij Resilience, flexibility and quality over scale: on 28-29 September, Property Forum 2026 will bring together real estate professionals, investors, developers, financiers and experts in Warsaw. Property Forum 2026 will take place on 28-29 September at the Sheraton Grand Warsaw. One of the main topics will be the resilience of real estate in the face of market change. Industry professionals will discuss challenges facing the office, hotel and logistics markets, as well as financing and the future of cities. The discussions will focus on building flexibility, energy, AI, demographics and the evolving needs of users. The first day of the event will conclude with the Prime Property Prize 2026 gala. The full two-day AGENDA is already available on the event’s official website, along with the option to REGISTER online. The real estate market is entering a period in which simply delivering a high-quality building in a good location may no longer be enough . Tenant expectations, working models, demographics, technology and investment financing are all changing. Requirements for energy efficiency are also becoming more stringent. The industry will discuss how to respond to these developments at Property Forum 2026. The event will take place on 28 and 29 September 2026 at the Sheraton Grand Warsaw. The organisers expect investors, developers, architects, representatives of financial institutions and local governments, as well as experts from Poland and across Central and Eastern Europe. The central theme of this year’s edition is the resilience and long-term relevance of real estate . The agenda will cover the impact of energy, infrastructure and artificial intelligence on asset values, the consequences of demographic change and migration, new ways of living and working, as well as the role of data centres, the living sector, urban regeneration and domestic capital. Czytaj więcej Major retail property deal: Appeninn buys Polish retail portfolio for over €100 million Offices are no longer just places to work One of the topics at Property Forum 2026 will be the future of the office sector : should the market build, modernise or repurpose? The discussion will examine whether there is still room for new office developments in Poland and which locations retain the greatest potential. Experts will also consider how to create buildings that remain competitive in terms of costs, energy performance and functionality over the next 10-15 years. The criteria guiding tenants’ decisions are also changing. Companies increasingly assess offices in terms of how the space supports their organisation, team collaboration and employee experience. Flexibility, workplace quality and community building are becoming increasingly important. This also means a changing role for property owners. Asset management after a building has been completed, responding to changes in tenants’ businesses and maintaining long-term relationships are all gaining importance. Property Forum 2025. Fot. PTWP Flexibility is becoming a pillar of resilience The issue is not limited to offices. A common thread running through many of the debates planned for Property Forum 2026 will be the ability to adapt real estate to new conditions. Ada Walentek of Nhood Services Poland highlights the importance of buildings that can be remodelled, extended or repurposed. From this perspective, the resilience of a property depends not only on its original design, but also on its subsequent management and carefully planned modernisation. The topic will feature in a forum discussion devoted to the flexibility, adaptability and interdisciplinary nature of real estate. Demographic change and the evolving profile of property users will provide the context for the debate. Cities are facing a similar challenge. The forum will provide an opportunity to discuss urban regeneration , the reuse of existing properties and the introduction of new functions into buildings. The debate about land availability will therefore be broadened to include the question of how already developed space can be used more efficiently. Property Forum 2025. Fot. PTWP Hotels: market growth does not mean every project will succeed A separate debate will focus on hotels. Its starting point will be the current position of a market that continues to grow while becoming increasingly selective. When new hotel projects are assessed, location and property standards are no longer the only decisive factors. Positioning, demand structure, the business model and the ability to generate revenue over the long term are becoming increasingly important. In practice, market growth does not automatically justify every new investment. This issue also forms part of a broader discussion about shifting from scale towards quality and adopting a more selective approach to projects. Warehouses compete for European operations Another area of discussion will be the warehouse, logistics and industrial market. The debate will focus on Poland’s position in the competition to attract companies’ European operations. Marek Dobrzycki, Head of Panattoni, emphasises that Poland’s competitive advantage is no longer based solely on costs. Its geographical location, infrastructure, access to labour and ability to support companies’ operations across Europe are also significant. The forum programme also includes topics related to energy and operational independence . Are energy efficiency and the ability to make buildings more self-sufficient becoming factors that directly influence their competitiveness and value? Property Forum 2025. Fot. PTWP Capital, investment and the question of who will own real estate Property Forum will also address the financing of the sector’s development. One of the debates will explore ways to increase the share of Polish capital in the real estate market. The agenda includes bonds, public markets, bank financing , funds and commercial REITs. The organisers will also examine the role of the Warsaw Stock Exchange, investment fund management companies, employee capital plans, investment firms, banks and private capital, while asking who will own Poland’s best properties ten years from now. On the first day, participants will also discuss Poland’s position among European economies and the factors that could encourage investors to commit capital to the country for the longer term. Czytaj więcej Poland’s logistics and industrial boom. The key investments to watch right now Prime Property Prize for the 16th time The Prime Property Prize 2026 gala will take place on the evening of 28 September. The awards will be presented for the 16th time. The competition recognises companies and projects that contribute to the development of Poland’s commercial and residential real estate markets . The judging criteria include investment quality, responsiveness to users’ needs, a long-term approach to asset creation and the impact of projects on cities and the economy. This year’s Property Forum will therefore cover almost the entire real estate decision-making chain – from land selection and financing to design and construction, followed by the management, modernisation or repurposing of existing assets. The central question linking the debates will be what types of real estate can retain their value amid economic, technological and demographic change. Property Forum 2025. Fot. PTWP More about Property Forum Property Forum is an event organised by PTWP Group and devoted to the real estate market in Poland and the CEE region. It brings together developers, investors, financial institutions, architects, property managers, experts and representatives of local government. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: A court sketch of Beau Lamarre-Condon during his double murder trial in the NSW supreme court. The 31-year-old has pleaded not guilty. Photograph: Rocco Fazzari/AAP View image in fullscreen A court sketch of Beau Lamarre-Condon during his double murder trial in the NSW supreme court. The 31-year-old has pleaded not guilty. Photograph: Rocco Fazzari/AAP New South Wales Beau Lamarre-Condon used friend to help fake cancer diagnosis before alleged double murder, court told Former NSW police officer, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington terrace in early 2024 Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong Thu 24 Sep 2026 22.18 EDT First published on Thu 24 Sep 2026 22.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Beau Lamarre-Condon “guilt-tripped” a friend into helping him fake a cancer diagnosis in the hope of explaining his erratic behaviour, months before the police officer allegedly murdered Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a Sydney court has heard. Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Baird, 26, and his partner, Davies, 29, with a police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. The 31-year-old has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. A close friend of Lamarre-Condon told the NSW supreme court on Friday that the policeman had become “infatuated” with Baird during a brief relationship. Beau Lamarre-Condon sized up surfboard bag against friend before allegedly murdering Sydney couple, court told Read more Baird ended the relationship in November 2023 after the accused went through his phone and deleted messages from other men, which made Lamarre-Condon “really upset”, Shae Davison told the jury. Lamarre-Condon then asked to stay at her house because he did not want to be alone, Davison said. The police officer arrived at her home with a backpack the next day and asked to send a message from her Instagram to Baird as “one last try to win Jesse back”, she told the court. But Lamarre-Condon did not want her to read the message, claiming there were medical details he did not want her to know. She didn’t want to do it initially but said: “He put a lot of pressure on me, he said he never asked anything of me, he’s so upset, can I help.” “He wore me down,” Davison said on Friday. “It felt like guilt-tripping to me and using my friendship to get what he wanted.” She agreed, on the condition Lamarre-Condon read out the text to her, while leaving out the medical details. When he read out the message, she asked him to delete parts that weren’t true, and it looked like he was typing and actioning her edits, she told the court. He then sent the note in a series of messages, and told her she was allowed to read it after 4 December 2023, when he told her he was set to undergo surgery. He left her home about an hour after he arrived. The 1,600-word Instagram note claimed Davison had gone to Westmead hospital with Lamarre-Condon. “He was told he had a cancerous tumour growing in his left shoulder joint/ligament area,” the text read out in court stated. “Worst-case scenario, it could result in … possibly having his arm amputated. “He was then immediately subscribed [sic] numerous medications … everyone knows these medications are some of the strongest you can be subscribed, which throw off your hormones massively, which throws off how a person can act in their day to day life.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion The friend told the jury she had not attended the hospital with Lamarre-Condon, nor did he clear this part of the text with her. The messages tried to justify the officer going through Baird’s phone and stated “this is very out of character for him”. “There is real love there, trust can be built back on that,” the note purportedly from Davison stated. “Even if you guys never hang out again, I know Beau wants to make things right.” View image in fullscreen Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird. Composite: Supplied by NSW supreme court The friend was unsure if Baird read the messages but said it was possible he had seen them through Instagram’s preview function. Lamarre-Condon later asked her to unsend the messages. She obliged and tried to ask him about the content of the messages but he did not want to talk about them. “He was quite annoyed, I could tell in his voice he was frustrated that I had [read them],” she said. It’s alleged Lamarre-Condon began planning to murder Baird in early 2024. The defence team has claimed the police officer was acting in self-defence after he disguised himself as an Uber Eats driver and entered Baird’s home on the day of the shootings. The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues. The video shows an unmanned surface combat vessel approaching the starboard side of the Liberian-flagged ship. The attack took place approximately 17 nautical miles from Cape Kaliakra, inside Bulgaria’s Exclusive Economic Zone. All 18 crew members, including 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians, were rescued and evacuated to Varna. The container ship sank around midnight. Maritime said the footage had been verified by three independent sources. Earlier, Chief of Defense Admiral Emil Eftimov said the attack on the vessel had come from the east. “We have sufficient information regarding the drones; footage may also emerge soon. We have shared the data we possess with the relevant competent authorities, both at the national level and within the alliance,” Eftimov added. The CONTSHIP JET was sailing from the Israeli port of Haifa to Constanța in Romania when it was attacked. The vessel sustained three breaches on its starboard side and was carrying 421 containers, 20 of which fell into the sea. Teams from the Executive Agency Maritime Administration inspected the damaged ship. After assessing its condition, the experts informed Regional Governor Mario Smurkov that no significant adverse effects on the marine environment or coastline were currently expected.
